newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve falls on liquidity outlook.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve falls on liquidity outlook.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were trading lower in late dealings on forex inflows, FRN expiries and FRN coupon payments on Friday that would pump liquidity into the cash-hungry market, dealers said.
"Depos and forex forwards have come down in late trade," said a trader at a foreign bank. "Forex inflows on Wednesday's fixing, FRN expiries and FRN coupon payments on Friday account for the drop."
The trader added that cash pumping by a state bank in the three-month period also contributed to the downward rate trend.
"I think liquidity will balance out tomorrow," he said.
The central bank drained overnight funds at 13.40 percent.
Ecu/drachma was trading firmer around 302.80 after the central bank drove the exchange rate higher at today's fixing.
A monetary source told Reuters that Greece shaved 10 basis points off the spreads of three-, five- and seven-year floaters to 40, 90 and 140 basis points respectively, a moneatry source told Reuters.

It also slashed three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates to 11 percent, 11.30 percent and 12 percent from 11.50 percent, 11.70 percent and 12.30 percent respectively effective November 12, the source said.
Greece will auction about 300 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds next week, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told reporters on Monday.
A finance ministry statement said 100 billion drachmas of five-year fixed coupon bonds, the first ever, will be auctioned.
The mark was quoted at 157.73/83 drachmas from Thursday's 157.815 fix, the dollar at 237.84/94 drachmas from 237.540 and the Ecu at 302.77/87 from 302.840 drachmas.
